### Symbols for complex systems

Symbols marked † are the subject's standard symbols and also have another meaning in a shared table. The conventions
section of the Complexity Science notation page lists each one with its meaning in that tutorial and says how the two
meanings are told apart where they meet.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\dot{\mathbf x} = \mathbf f(\mathbf x)$, $\mathbf x_{n+1} = \mathbf F(\mathbf x_n)$ | a flow (continuous time) and a map (discrete time) on a state space |
| $\varphi^t(\mathbf x)$ | the state at time $t$ of the flow started at $\mathbf x$ |
| $s_i(t) \in S_i$, $\mathbf s = (s_1, \dots, s_N)$, $\mathcal S$ | state of element $i$ at time $t$ in its state set; a microstate; the set $S_1 \times \dots \times S_N$ of microstates |
| $w^\alpha_{ij}(t)$, $\mathbf W^\alpha(t)$ | weight of the interaction of type $\alpha$ from element $j$ to element $i$ at time $t$; the matrix of these weights |
| $\pi : \mathcal S \to \mathcal Y$ | a coarse-graining: the map from microstates to the macrostates $\mathcal Y$ of a level of description |
| $m$ | magnetisation per element, $m = \frac1N\sum_i s_i$ for states $s_i = \pm1$, the standard order parameter |
| $\mathbf x^*$ † | fixed point, $\mathbf f(\mathbf x^*) = \mathbf 0$ or $\mathbf F(\mathbf x^*) = \mathbf x^*$ |
| $\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \dots$, $\lambda_{\max}$ † | Lyapunov exponents of a trajectory; the largest one |
| $\mu$ † | bifurcation parameter of a family of flows or maps |
| $\mathcal B_A$ † | basin of attraction of an attracting set $A$ |
| $\omega(\mathbf x)$ † | $\omega$-limit set of $\mathbf x$: the limits of $\varphi^{t_k}(\mathbf x)$ with $t_k \to \infty$ |
| $\Sigma$ †, $\mathbf P_\Sigma$ | Poincaré section (a hypersurface transversal to the flow); the Poincaré (first-return) map on it |
| $r_k$, $r_\infty$; $\delta_F$, $\alpha_F$ | parameter of the $k$-th period doubling and of its accumulation; Feigenbaum's constants $4.6692\dots$ and $-2.5029\dots$ |
| $\sigma$, $\rho$, $\beta$ † | parameters of the Lorenz system $\dot x = \sigma(y - x)$, $\dot y = x(\rho - z) - y$, $\dot z = xy - \beta z$ |
| $h_{\mathrm{KS}}$ | Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of a dynamical system |
| $N(\varepsilon)$ | number of boxes of side $\varepsilon$ needed to cover a set |
| $D_0$ † | box-counting dimension, $\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}\log N(\varepsilon)/\log(1/\varepsilon)$ |
| $C(\varepsilon)$, $D_2$ † | correlation sum: fraction of pairs of points closer than $\varepsilon$; correlation dimension, $\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}\log C(\varepsilon)/\log\varepsilon$ |
| $D_q$ | generalised (Rényi) dimension of order $q$, with $D_0$ and $D_2$ as special cases |
| $T_i$, $r_i$ †; $D_s$ | similarities of an iterated function system and their ratios, always indexed; the similarity dimension, the root of $\sum_ir_i^{D_s} = 1$ |
| $M(R)$ †, $D_f$ | mass (number of particles) within radius $R$ of a centre; mass dimension, $M(R) \propto R^{D_f}$ |
| $x_{(k)}$, $\zeta$ | the $k$-th largest of a sample (rank $k$); Zipf exponent, $x_{(k)} \propto k^{-\zeta}$ |
| $\nu$ | probability of a reducing jump of a sample-space-reducing process |
| $D_{\mathrm{KS}}$ | Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between an empirical and a fitted distribution function |
| $H$ †, $\mathcal F(n)$ | Hurst exponent, $\operatorname{Var}S_n \propto n^{2H}$; detrended fluctuation at window size $n$ |
| $c(k)$, $\sigma_\infty^2$ | autocovariance $\operatorname{Cov}(\xi_t, \xi_{t + k})$ of a stationary sequence; long-run variance $\sum_kc(k)$ |
| $Y = Y_0X^b$, $b$ | allometric scaling law and its exponent; $X$ a body mass $M$ or a population $N$ |
| $u_n$, $f_n$; $T$ | probability that a random walk is at its starting point at step $n$, and that it returns there for the first time at step $n$; the first return time |
| $\mathbf P$, $P_{ij}$; $\boldsymbol\pi$ † | transition matrix of a Markov chain, $P_{ij} = \mathbb P(X_{n + 1} = j \mid X_n = i)$; a stationary distribution, $\boldsymbol\pi\mathbf P = \boldsymbol\pi$ |
| $\mathbf Q$, $Q_{ij}$ | rate matrix of a continuous-time Markov chain: the rate of jumps from $i$ to $j \neq i$; master equation $\dot{\mathbf p} = \mathbf p\mathbf Q$ |
| $b_n$, $d_n$ | birth and death rates of a birth-death process in state $n$ |
| $Z_n$, $G(z)$, $q$ †, $Y$ | generation sizes, offspring generating function, extinction probability and total progeny of a branching process |
| $p(x) \propto x^{-\alpha}$, $x \geq x_{\min}$ † | power-law density with exponent $\alpha$ above the lower cut-off $x_{\min}$ |
| $S(\alpha_s, \beta_s, \gamma, \delta)$ | stable law with index $\alpha_s \in (0, 2]$, skewness $\beta_s$, scale $\gamma$ and location $\delta$ |
| $\mu$ †, $\ell_i$ | tail exponent of the jump lengths of a Lévy flight, $\mathbb P(\ell_i > l) = (l/\ell_0)^{-\mu}$; the jump lengths |
| $\kappa$ | tail exponent of a multiplicative process, the positive root of $\mathbb E[\Lambda^\kappa] = 1$ for the random factor $\Lambda$ |
| $\operatorname{Beta}(A, B)$ | beta distribution, with density $x^{A - 1}(1 - x)^{B - 1}/\mathrm B(A, B)$ on $(0, 1)$ |
| $\bar F(x)$ | complementary distribution function $\mathbb P(X > x)$ |
| $G = (V, E)$, $N$, $M$ † | a graph with node set $V$ and edge set $E$; its numbers of nodes $N = \lvert V\rvert$ and edges $M = \lvert E\rvert$ |
| $\mathbf A$, $A_{ij}$ | adjacency matrix; $A_{ij} = 1$ if node $i$ links to node $j$ |
| $k_i$, $\langle k\rangle$ † | degree of node $i$; mean degree of a network |
| $P(k)$ † | degree distribution: the fraction of nodes with degree $k$ |
| $C_i$, $C$ † | clustering coefficient of node $i$; the clustering coefficient of a network |
| $d_{ij}$, $\ell$ † | shortest-path distance between nodes $i$ and $j$; average shortest-path length of a network |
| $\mathbf L = \mathbf D - \mathbf A$ † | graph Laplacian, with $\mathbf D$ the diagonal matrix of degrees |
| $p$, $p_c$ † | occupation or link probability; its critical (percolation) value |
| $\theta(p)$, $P_\infty$, $n_s$ | percolation probability (the origin lies in an infinite cluster); share of sites in the largest cluster of a finite lattice; clusters of size $s$ per site |
| $\Pi_L(p)$ | probability that a lattice of side $L$ has a spanning cluster |
| $Y_L(p) \approx L^a\Phi((p - p_c)L^{1/\nu})$ | finite-size scaling form with scaling function $\Phi$; $\nu$ the correlation-length exponent |
| $R(p)$ | real-space renormalisation map of an occupation probability |
| $\tau_{\mathrm{int}}$, $z$ | integrated autocorrelation time of a Monte Carlo series; dynamic exponent, $\tau_{\mathrm{int}} \propto L^z$ at criticality |
| $U_L$ | Binder cumulant $1 - \langle m^4\rangle/(3\langle m^2\rangle^2)$ |
| $\rho(t)$, $\lambda$ †, $\varepsilon$ | density of active sites of an absorbing-state process; infection rate of the contact process; distance from an absorbing transition |
| $\theta_j$, $\omega_j$ | phase and natural frequency of oscillator $j$ |
| $K$, $K_c$ † | coupling strength of oscillators; its critical value at the onset of synchronization |
| $r e^{i\psi} = \frac1N\sum_j e^{i\theta_j}$ † | Kuramoto order parameter: its modulus $r$ measures coherence, $\psi$ is the mean phase |
| $s$, $P(s) \propto s^{-\tau}$ † | avalanche size; its distribution and exponent |
| $\sigma$ † | branching ratio: the mean number of offspring of one event |
| $R_0$ | basic reproduction number of an epidemic |
| $h$ † | entropy rate of a stationary source, $\lim_{n \to \infty}H(X_1, \dots, X_n)/n$ |
| $E$ † | excess entropy of a stationary source |
| $T_{X \to Y}$ | transfer entropy from the process $X$ to the process $Y$ |

The entropy $H(X)$, the mutual information $I(X; Y)$ and the Kullback-Leibler divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ are those of
the probability and statistics table.
